title: Non-overlapping Intervals Problem

notes: Intervals that touch at an endpoint are non-overlapping; for example, [1,2] and [2,3] may both remain.
The greedy strategy keeps an interval with the earliest finishing time whenever an overlap is found, because that leaves the most room for future intervals.

content.problemStatement:
With an array of intervals `intervals` where `intervals[i] = [start_i, end_i]`, output *the smallest number of intervals you need to remove to make the rest of the intervals non-overlapping*.

**Note** that intervals which only touch at a point are **non-overlapping**. As an example, `[1, 2]` and `[2, 3]` are non-overlapping.

**Example 1:**

```
Input: intervals = [[1,2],[2,3],[3,4],[1,3]]
Output: 1
Explanation: [1,3] can be removed and the rest of the intervals are non-overlapping.
```

**Example 2:**

```
Input: intervals = [[1,2],[1,2],[1,2]]
Output: 2
Explanation: You need to remove two [1,2] to make the rest of the intervals non-overlapping.
```

**Example 3:**

```
Input: intervals = [[1,2],[2,3]]
Output: 0
Explanation: You don't need to remove any of the intervals since they're already non-overlapping.
```

**Constraints:**

* `1 <= intervals.length <= 10^5`
* `intervals[i].length == 2`
* `-5 * 10^4 <= start_i < end_i <= 50002 * 10^4`

notes: Inputs are one JSON-serialised argument array; the supplied language drivers parse that format.
The overlap test is start < previousEnd because touching endpoints are explicitly allowed.
The greedy exchange argument is that among overlapping choices, keeping the interval with the earliest end cannot reduce the number of intervals that can be selected later.
solution.approach: Sort intervals by increasing end time and greedily keep the next interval whose start is at or after the end of the last kept interval. Every overlap is counted as one removal. This is equivalent to maximizing the number of non-overlapping intervals (activity selection).

better.complexity: O(n^2) time after sorting and O(n) space.
better.description: Sort by start time and perform dynamic programming: for each interval, either skip it or keep it and transition to the best compatible interval. This reduces the exponential search but is still more work than necessary.

optimal.complexity: O(n log n) time for sorting and O(n) worst-case auxiliary space, depending on the language sorting implementation.
optimal.description: Sort by end time and greedily keep every interval that starts at or after the end of the last kept interval. This is the classic activity-selection greedy algorithm. Whenever an interval overlaps the current choice, removing the one with the later end is always safe because the earlier-ending interval leaves at least as much room for every future interval.

bruteForce.complexity: O(2^n * n^2) time and O(n) auxiliary space.
bruteForce.description: Try every subset of intervals, keep the largest subset whose intervals do not overlap, and return n minus that maximum. This is useful only for very small inputs because there are 2^n subsets.

solution.spaceComplexity: O(n) worst-case auxiliary space due to the sorting implementation; the greedy scan itself uses O(1) extra variables.
